newsitem.title: NORWAY: RGI criticised before merger with Aker.
newsitem.headline: RGI criticised before merger with Aker.

text.p: A Norwegian brokerage has questioned the cashflow capability of investment group RGI (Antilles) n.v. prior to its proposed merger with engineering and offshore group Aker ASA.
Fondsfinans, in a comment on fisheries-based RGI published by three major newspapers on Wednesday, said one Aker share should equal 2.40 RGI shares rather than 2.15 as the proposed deal says.

Aker shareholders will vote on the proposed merger at an extraordinary meeting on Thursday. The deal is expected to go through because RGI controls more than 40 percent of Aker voting shares and has won support from other major shareholders.
But Fondsfinans, adding a critical voice to a choir of praise in Norway for the planned merger, said it was sceptical of RGI's Antilles-based parent company.

"The cashflow is not particularly robust in case of a negative development in the markets," the report said. "The ability to pay a dividend on the basis of the running cashflow will...be strictly limited."
A Fondsfinans analyst confirmed the brokerhouse had written the comment, dated Monday.

Financial daily Dagens Naeringsliv said it was unfortunate for the public debate that industry leaders had refrained from questioning the merger proposal itself or RGI co-founder Kjell Inge Roekke, a charismatic entrepreneur who started buying Aker shares aggressively last February.
"Why does nobody want to challenge Kjell Inge Roekke in public?" the newspaper asked in an editorial. "The answer is probably that almost everyone has everything to lose from turning against him."

"While information on Aker is relatively easy to come by, there is a considerable lack of information on RGI," it said. "On the basis of this, we feel the swap rate should have been 2.40 RGI shares per Aker share."

The proposed merger will bring together one of Norway's oldest companies with a newcomer on the corporate scene. Aker was founded in 1841 while RGI, which has quickly become the world's largest white-fish fishing and processing operation, was listed on the Oslo Bourse only this year.

The merger proposal was presented by the boards of Aker and RGI on October 1. The combined company, Aker RGI ASA, will have annual revenues of 19 billion crowns and a market capitalisation of nine billion crowns.

The company will focus on three core areas -- seafood, cement and oil and gas - - but will look for other areas to stretch its newly-found financial muscle, according to Bjoern Rune Gjelsten, Aker chairman and chairman-designated of the new joint board.
Gjelsten is co-owner of RGI with Roekke, who will have a shareholding in the new company of 33 percent.
